memories.content: The user decided to keep the Node.js engine floor at version 20 because the project uses `crypto.hash()`, which was added in Node.js 20.12 and 21.7, and they do not want to add compatibility shims.
The project's tests require Node.js 20 or newer because they use `crypto.hash()`, which is not available in Node.js 18.
The user standardized on pnpm in January 2026 for package management in their project.

The user adopted the change to remove the Node.js 18 entry from the test matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, set `engines.node` to `>=20`, and added a requirement for Node.js 20 or newer (specifically mentioning `crypto.hash` and its availability from 20.12) to the README.
The user adopted the change to update the install block in the README to use `pnpm install` and the scripts section to reference `pnpm test` and `pnpm build`.
The user's orders report is timing out.
The user decided to add an index on `orders(customer_id, created_at)` to address the orders report timing out.
The user's migration files follow the naming convention `<timestamp>_<snake_description>.ts` and are located in `db/migrations`.
The `orders` table in production has approximately 40 million rows.
The user experienced a problem in December where a plain `CREATE INDEX` locked writes for several minutes on the `orders` table.
The user's project's migration runner (`db/run-migrations.ts`) wraps every migration in `BEGIN/COMMIT` transactions.
The user's project's migration runner supports an escape hatch where a migration module can export `disableTransaction = true` to execute with autocommit, bypassing the `BEGIN/COMMIT` wrapper.

The user adopted the assistant's suggestion to add `disableTransaction = true` to the new migration file `db/migrations/20260304_add_orders_customer_created_idx.ts` because `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction block.
The user decided to add a comment at the top of the migration file explaining why `disableTransaction` is present.
The user's local database now has the `orders_customer_created_idx` index.
The orders report query now uses an Index Scan on the new index instead of a Seq Scan plus Sort.
The user is on the on-call rotation this week (2026-01-20) and wants to keep pull requests small.
The user wants the `Aggregate()` function to produce a stable order, specifically by sorting by label name.

The user's `TestAggregate` in `internal/metrics` was failing on CI due to non-deterministic map iteration order in Go, which was fixed by sorting the keys before building the result slice in `Aggregate()`.
The user wants the race detector (`-race`) to be included in every CI run for `go test`, even if it increases the job duration.
The user's CI job for `go test` now includes the `-race` flag, increasing its duration from 1 minute 10 seconds to 2 minutes 40 seconds, and no races were reported.
The user's Vercel bill for their portfolio site was $41 last month (April 2026), primarily due to image optimization bandwidth. This cost is considered excessive for a static site.
The user is moving to Poznań next month (June 2026) and is reviewing all recurring costs.
The user decided to move their portfolio site to Cloudflare Pages because they do not need a runtime image optimizer, as their images are static.

The user's portfolio site now uses `output: 'export'` and `images: { unoptimized: true }` in `next.config.ts`, causing `next/image` to emit plain `img` tags pointing to pre-sized files in `public/images`.
The user's portfolio site now has 1x and 2x image variants generated with `sharp` in a build step using `scripts/resize-images.ts`.
The user's static build for the portfolio site deploys to Cloudflare Pages from the main branch, with the project named 'portfolio' and a custom domain pointed at it.
The user's old Vercel project for the portfolio site has been paused.
The user decided to keep the Vercel project paused for a month (until June 2026) to ensure nothing is broken before deleting it after their move.
The contact form for the user's portfolio site now posts to a Cloudflare Pages Function at `functions/api/contact.ts`.
The user's weather ETL job, `etl/weather_daily.py`, written in pandas, fails with a MemoryError when processing a 12 GB parquet dump.
The user decided to rewrite the `etl/weather_daily.py` script using Polars to address a MemoryError, aiming to keep the output identical for downstream dashboards that read `daily_weather.parquet`.

When using Polars, `sink_parquet` can cause a MemoryError by running the entire plan in memory. The fix is to combine `collect(engine='streaming')` with `sink_parquet`, as the streaming engine is opt-in per query in Polars 1.x.
The user's rewritten Polars script for `etl/weather_daily.py` processes a 12 GB input with a peak memory usage of 2.1 GB when using the streaming engine.
When migrating from pandas to Polars, if downstream readers expect `datetime64[ns]` for dates, Polars' default Date type needs to be cast to Datetime to maintain compatibility.
The user's new `daily_weather.parquet` file, generated by the Polars script, has 3,652 rows and the same column set as the pandas version.
The user initiated the full ETL job and went for lunch.

The user's MusicPlayer project, a Kotlin app using media3, experienced playback stopping when the screen locked on their Pixel 8 (Android 14), but worked fine on an older Samsung device running Android 12.

To fix playback stopping when the screen locks on Android 14, the user's `PlaybackService` in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` needed `android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback"` and the `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK` permission. This was identified by a `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` in logcat on the Pixel about 10 seconds after the screen locked.

The user committed the change to declare the `mediaPlayback` foreground service type for Android 14 with the commit message "Declare the mediaPlayback foreground service type for Android 14". The user prefers commit messages in the imperative mood, without emojis or a 'fix:' prefix, as they do not use conventional commits.
The user decided to drop the Samsung device from their test devices and set the `minSdk` to 33 in `app/build.gradle.kts`, believing that few users run the app on Android versions below 13.
When setting `minSdk = 33`, the user removed two `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 31` guards from the code because they became redundant.
The user is starting a Rust rewrite of the token-saver CLI, with Windows as the primary target.
The user prefers to use `clap derive` for argument parsing in the Rust rewrite of the token-saver CLI, valuing the typed struct over saving a dependency.

The user's `proxy` subcommand, when running a wrapped command through the shell on Windows, was slow due to `powershell -Command` loading the user profile, which took about 1.9 seconds. The fix was to use `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command`, reducing the spawn time to about 180 ms and the end-to-end `rtk proxy git status` time from 2.1 s to 0.3 s.
The user decided to keep the `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` fix for the `proxy` subcommand and requested a comment in the code to explain the reason for its inclusion.

On April 2, 2026, a deploy of shopfront at 14:10 broke checkout for 25 minutes because Stripe webhooks all returned 400 errors. The issue was resolved when the user manually set the correct environment variable.
The user's Stripe webhook secret for production is stored in the 'shopfront-prod' 1Password vault under the Stripe item.
The user decided to write up the incident in docs/incidents/2026-04-02-stripe-webhooks.md, including a link to the deploy checklist.
The user's project now includes a startup check in settings.py that fails fast with a clear message if any required secret is empty, preventing the container from starting if secrets are missing.

The user's deploy checklist in docs/deploy.md now includes `python manage.py check --deploy` and a `scripts/verify-env.sh` step. The script compares variable names in .env.example against the target host's environment and exits with an error if any are missing.
The user's monorepo linting process, which uses ESLint, Prettier, and an import plugin, currently takes 90 seconds.
The user decided to switch from ESLint and Prettier to Biome for linting and formatting.
The user's project will no longer use the `no-cycle` rule from `eslint-plugin-import` because Biome does not have an equivalent, but this is acceptable as `madge` catches these issues in CI.
The user prefers to maintain 100-column lines and double quotes for code formatting.
The user wants the formatter to be run once over the entire repository in its own commit to preserve `git blame` readability.
To ensure Biome ignores files correctly, the user needs to set `vcs.enabled: true` and `useIgnoreFile: true` in `biome.json`.
The user's setlist app needs to update live on everyone's phone during band rehearsals, which happen on Thursdays, because songs are frequently reordered mid-session.
The user prefers WebSockets for the setlist app's live updates because they need updates to be instant, especially since they play bass and have their hands full.
The user decided to use WebSockets on the Hono server for the setlist app.
On 2026-08-13, the user tested the setlist app on their iPhone at a rehearsal with the Ulica Cicha band, and it stopped receiving updates until reloaded.

The user's setlist app experienced an issue where iOS Safari silently drops idle WebSockets when the tab is in the background or the screen dims. The fix implemented was to send a client-side ping every 20 seconds and reconnect with backoff if no pong is received within 5 seconds, also re-subscribing to the setlist on reconnect to fetch any missed reorders.
The user wants the setlist app, with the WebSocket heartbeat fix, to be shipped before Thursday.

The user plans to write a migration to reinterpret existing local timestamps as 'Europe/Warsaw' and convert them to UTC.
The user set a deadline of March 29, 2026, for implementing the UTC storage and migration, as it is the next clock change.
The user plans to add a test that runs the sync job across a DST boundary using a fake clock.
